summary: Arizona State University's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program (Phase III, 2024–2030) supports 600 young Africans through in-person and online degrees and certificates focused on innovation and technology.
covers: Full scholarships for selected in-person and online degree and certificate pathways.
Leadership, career and entrepreneurship support focused on innovation and technology.
600 scholars across the programme's current phase.
eligibility: Young people from African countries who meet the pathway's academic and financial-need criteria.
Pathways differ, and some carry specific conditions — recent Innovation and Technology cohorts included a residency requirement in Rwanda.
Read the current call for age limits and level (bachelor's, master's or certificate).
how_to_apply: Read the current call on the ASU Mastercard Foundation Scholars website and pick a pathway.
Apply through the programme's application portal before the call's deadline (the most recent call closed on 29 March).
Prepare academic records, essays and evidence of financial need.
watch_out: Online and in-person pathways have different conditions — know which you are applying for.
Pathway rules change between cohorts; do not rely on last year's requirements.
Apply only through the official ASU site.
